name: com.redstonemarkets/redstone
title: Redstone Markets
description: Performance, risk, comparisons, backtests and screening for US stocks, ETFs and closed-end funds.

tools.name: get_security_metrics
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how a single US stock, ETF or closed-end fund has performed or how risky it is: YTD, 1-year and 5-year annualized returns, max drawdown, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, beta, alpha and dividend yield, with a 1Y/5Y chart. End-of-day data for US large and mid caps, major foreign stocks, US ETFs and closed-end funds. Not for intraday quotes, news, earnings, fundamentals or price targets.

ticker.description: US ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, VOO or BRK.B

tools.name: compare_securities
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to compare 2 to 5 US stocks, ETFs or closed-end funds side by side (e.g. "VOO vs QQQ", "SCHD or VYM?"): returns, drawdown, volatility, Sharpe, beta, dividend yield and how correlated they are, with an overlaid 1Y/5Y chart. End-of-day data for US large and mid caps, major foreign stocks, US ETFs and closed-end funds. Not for intraday quotes or recommendations on what to buy.

items.description: US ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, VOO or BRK.B

tickers.description: Tickers to compare, in the order the user named them

tools.name: backtest_portfolio
tools.description: Use this when the user describes a portfolio of US stocks, ETFs or closed-end funds with weights (e.g. "60% VTI, 40% BND", "equal parts AAPL, MSFT, NVDA") and wants to know how it would have done or how risky it is: returns over YTD, 1 year and 5 years (rebalanced quarterly), max drawdown, volatility, Sharpe, beta vs SPY, dividend yield and the correlation between holdings, charted against SPY, with a link that opens it on Redstone to save. 2 to 20 holdings. Not for live brokerage accounts, trading or allocation advice.

ticker.description: US ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, VOO or BRK.B

weight.description: Relative weight, e.g. 60 for 60%. Weights are rescaled to sum to 100%, so equal weights can all be 1

tools.name: screen_securities
tools.description: Use this when the user wants a ranked list of US stocks, ETFs or closed-end funds by a performance, risk or dividend yield metric, optionally within a sector or fund category (e.g. "lowest volatility dividend ETFs", "highest yielding bond ETFs", "highest Sharpe tech stocks this year", "municipal bond closed-end funds with the smallest drawdown"). Covers about 2,900 US-listed stocks, about 1,700 US ETFs and about 200 closed-end funds, end-of-day. Not for fundamentals (P/E, revenue), news or buy recommendations.

type.description: stock, etf, or all (stocks and ETFs together); cef screens closed-end funds, which all leaves out

sector.description: Case-insensitive match on a stock's GICS sector (e.g. Information Technology, Health Care, Energy, Financials) or a fund's category (ETFs: e.g. Dividend, Bonds, Treasury, Large Cap Growth, Emerging Markets, Gold; closed-end funds: e.g. Municipal Bonds, High Yield Bonds, Preferred Stock, Covered Call, Private Companies)

sortBy.description: Metric to rank by. For lowest risk, sort volatility1yPct ascending, maxDrawdown1yPct descending (closest to 0) or beta1y ascending

filters.description: Optional bounds in each metric's own units, e.g. {metric: 'beta1y', max: 1}. maxDrawdown1yPct is negative, so a drawdown smaller than 20% is {metric: 'maxDrawdown1yPct', min: -20}

tools.name: search_portfolios
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to see real portfolios to learn from or copy (e.g. "show me low-drawdown dividend portfolios", "portfolios that hold SCHD", "the best risk-adjusted portfolios on Redstone"): the public portfolios Redstone's users built and shared, and Redstone's model portfolios, with past-year returns, risk and yield. Describe the kind of portfolio with the figure filters where one fits; nameIncludes only matches names, so keep it for themes no figure captures, such as "AI". Up to 10 results. Not for the user's own brokerage account or for recommending a portfolio to buy.

nameIncludes.description: Words to look for in portfolio names, e.g. 'dividend' or 'AI'; any one matching is enough

items.description: US ticker symbol, e.g. AAPL, VOO or BRK.B

madeBy.description: community: portfolios users built and shared; redstone: Redstone's model portfolios

maxDrawdownNoWorseThanPct.description: Keep portfolios whose worst fall over the past year was no deeper than this, e.g. -10

order.description: desc puts the highest first; for drawdown the highest is the shallowest

tools.name: get_portfolio
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one public Redstone portfolio, usually a search_portfolios result: its holdings with each one's own figures, its returns over YTD, 1 year and 5 years, max drawdown, volatility, Sharpe, beta and dividend yield, charted against SPY. Not for a portfolio the user describes (use backtest_portfolio) or private portfolios.

portfolio.description: The portfolio's Redstone url, as search_portfolios returns it
